correctness.rationale: In the fixed-diagonal affine space, the off-diagonal coordinate isometry up to factor sqrt(2) preserves both nearest points and the max-entry size of differences. For k=n-2 and any r>0, the two contrast eigenvalues are 2(1-c^2) and k(1-a^2)/(k-1); the two-constant sector has matrix with diagonal 2c^2, ka^2 and off-diagonal -sqrt(2k)ca. Its determinant is zero and trace positive. The kernel is precisely span(1,1,r,...,r). Differentiating the simple zero eigenvalue in zero-diagonal directions gives the halfspace with inward normal q_ij=v_i v_j; its exterior-direction projection has tangent-plane linear part I-qq^T/||q||_2^2. The (1,2) row has nonnegative diagonal, negative other entries, and absolute sum exactly 1+F_k(r). At the boundary this is a directional tangent-plane calculation, not a claim of an ordinary two-sided derivative of the projector. For each fixed direction, the scaled convex sets increase to a dense subset of the tangent cone as the scale decreases; bounded nearest points therefore converge to the unique tangent-cone nearest point. A common exterior shift of two directions realizing the row signs yields two distinct nearby finite inputs and their ratio limit. F_k has a positive attained maximum since it is positive at r=1, tends to -1 at zero and to 0 at infinity. At r=s/sqrt(k), F_k/k converges uniformly on compact s intervals to s^2/(2+4s^2+s^4); the small-s numerator bound and large-s quartic denominator bound trap all maximizing sequences away from both tails. Differentiating in s^2 gives the unique limiting maximizer 2^(1/4) for s and maximum (2-sqrt(2))/4. Firm nonexpansivity in n(n-1)/2 independent coordinates bounds the full Lipschitz modulus from above at linear order, not by the particular family constant.
residual_risks: The distinguished-row value need not optimize all elliptope normals; no unrestricted sharp finite or leading constant and no exact finite-pair attainment are certified.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The elliptope has nonsmooth points (e.g. at the all-ones rank-one matrix, distinct nonproportional off-diagonal outward normals arise from different kernel contrasts), so the all-normal sharp lower bound for globally smooth bodies does not cover it. Its simple-kernel smooth normals are constrained by q_ij=v_i v_j. Neither spectral-ball nor PSD-cone projection enforces the same affine slice.

value.rationale: For a standard operation in correlation repair, the theorem determines the growth order of a natural measure of worst-case individual-entry error and exhibits the exact local geometry that causes it. Realizing rank deficiency while maintaining the whole unit diagonal is a relevant constraint, not an arbitrary parameter restriction. The optimized witness makes the lower bound useful even though the full sharp constant is open.
residual_risks: Worst-case inputs in the stated affine space are not restricted to PSD or to entries in [-1,1]; no performance conclusion for a restricted set of empirical inputs is made.
